Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Ireland's reply. The Pakistan players are out in the middle now. Followed by Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie who will open for the hosts. Shaheen Afridi gets the new ball in hand. Here we go..
... The Run Chase ...

Ireland were exceptional with the ball throughout the innings barring the final two overs, one might say. They had everything under control from the get-go when Mohammad Rizwan had to walk back cheaply for just a single. Then came a fightback from Saim Ayub and the Pakistani skipper, as they stitched a 85-run stand to get their innings back on track, but once this pair was broken no one really could put their hand up with the bat. Some good tight bowling from Ireland put the opposition under tremendous pressure once again, and the host cashed in on it as well by picking up three wickets in just 7 deliveries. This is when it felt like Pakistan will be finishing on an under-par score, but in the end, Pakistan found a way somehow to finish on a high. Craig Young was the pick of the bowlers for Ireland surely. Although, now for the visitors it is all about carrying the momentum. Will it be enough though to put the Irish hopes to bed? Do join us shortly for the second essay to find out.

WOW! What a recovery this has been from Pakistan. A wonderful cameo from Iftikhar Ahmed of 37 runs off just 15 deliveries with a valuable help from Shaheen Afridi has helped them to get to the magical number that Babar Azam mentioned during the toss. 183 is what Ireland have to chase down to take a lead in this series. Quite, a tall mountain to climb. How costly will the final two overs prove to be for them.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities. The two Pakistani openers Mohammad Rizwan and Saim Ayub walk out to the 22 yards. Ireland players have already taken their respective field positions. It will be Mark Adair to begin the proceedings with the new ball. And, here we go! Uh, oh! A halt first up as there's some issue with the sightscreen. The issue is resolved and Saim Ayub has taken his stance. Let's play...
Right then, both the teams are out now and have lined-up for their respective national anthems. It is going to be Pakistan's first followed by the one of the hosts.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Saim Ayub, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Shadab Khan, Azam Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah and Abbas Afridi.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Mark Adair, Andy Balbirnie, Curtis Campher, Gareth Delany, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), George Dockrell, Barry McCarthy, Ben White, Craig Young.
TOSS -  The coin goes up and lands in favour of Ireland. They will BOWL first.

Paul Stirling leading the side, and he also leads with the bat, the intent he shows is ideal for a T20 contest. Then you add some young-blood energy in the middle-order, with some quality bowling attack, then one can even say that Ireland are a complete package, but can they bring their A-game against one of the best? Only time will tell. Stay tuned as the toss is just around the corner.

It is not often that these two sides meet each-other, in fact, they only encountered once before this series that too back in 2009 for a T20I game. Ireland have certainly grown as a cricketing side over the years, and it will be very interesting to see how they come up against a formidable Pakistani side, because when it comes to T20 Pakistan is certainly up there. It's just that they find it a tad difficult to be consistent game in and game out. Although, Babar Azam is trying his best to change the attitude of the players, and with this series is hoping to put his team in the right direction. Babar Azam has plenty of quality players at his disposal and will hope to have an upper-hand in this game for the majority of the period, but this Ireland team is something else at home.

Hello and a warm welcome to all! We know that one expects an Indian T20 League to be covered at this time of the day, but as that league is into its business end. Our attention now has started to shift towards the upcoming T20 World Cup which is just around the corner. Also, Ireland and Pakistan have realised that their it is time to kick-start their preparations for the same. The two sides go up against each other in a 3-match T20I series, in Ireland's backyard and we are here to kick-start this series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The T20 World Cup 2024 is on the horizon, prompting teams to engage in bilateral series for preparation. Pakistan embarks on a tour of Ireland for a three-match T20I series, aiming to recover from a drawn home series against a weakened New Zealand side. Led by the experienced duo of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan, Pakistan's batting lineup exudes stability. Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman add firepower at the top, while Azam Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, and Imad Wasim strengthen the middle order. With a formidable pace attack featuring Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Naseem Shah, and Mohammad Amir, Pakistan boasts depth and versatility in bowling. Wasim's spin expertise and Shadab Khan's all-round skills further enhance their chances, making them clear favorites for the series. Ireland sees this series as an invaluable opportunity to gain vital match practice and potentially spring surprises. Paul Stirling leads the team both tactically and with the bat, alongside Andy Balbirnie, as they seek to provide explosive starts. The middle order boasts quality players like Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker, and Curtis Campher, eager to leave their mark ahead of the major event. Mark Adair and Barry McCarthy spearhead the pace attack, supported by Craig Young, while Ben White assumes the role of their key spinner. With a balanced unit, Ireland aims to seize every opportunity and pose a challenge to the formidable Pakistan side. This sets the stage for an intriguing contest, and fans eagerly await to witness which team emerges victorious.
